about: The agent roster: thirteen specialists under the orchestrator. Read by .claude/hooks/_gate.py
(ROSTER: who a payload's agent_type may name), scripts/team.py (who is switched on, and the
exact words a switched-off agent answers with), and scripts/validate_agent_contracts.py
(every agent here has a file, with the model given here, and a switched-off one holds only
Read, Glob and Grep). The roll call and the status line name whoever the transcript shows
was dispatched and skip a dispatch a gate refused, so they need no copy of this list.
`lane` is the parenthesis in the NOT SWITCHED ON lines that docs/FOR-TAYLOR.md quotes.
`phase` is the blueprint phase; null means outside the blueprint. `via` names a deviation
that can switch the agent on by itself (docs/DEVIATIONS.md).
`delivery: true` marks the one agent allowed to run scripts/docs_edit.py and `privacy: true`
the one allowed to run scripts/privacy_review.py. The hooks that enforce them hardcode the
same names on purpose, and the guardrail self-test checks the two still agree.

orchestrator.lane: dispatch, reality-checker, deviation memos, Needs Your Input

agents.name: RUTH
agents.specialty: Factual management records drafted privately; Taylor classifies, never RUTH

agents.name: ATLAS
agents.specialty: Projects, co-owners and deadlines; current versus historical company knowledge

agents.name: CLEO

agents.name: JUNE

agents.name: PENN
agents.specialty: Commission, promoter and event ROI tracking; stale leads with Moreen

agents.name: TALLY
agents.specialty: Product and games mix, repeat guests; only if Taylor resumes Phase 6

about: Mike's half of 'is this agent switched on': what is built and accepted on the build
machine. A key is a phase ('phase 2') or a deviation ('D-4'); `accepted` is the date
its acceptance passed on fixtures, and `evidence` the report that shows it (the report
stays on the build machine). A key that is absent is not built. This file is code: it
changes only on the machine state/BUILD_MACHINE names.
